subject: humanities
passage: In true fresco, a method used by many Italian Renaissance painters, pigment is brushed onto fresh, wet plaster. As the plaster dries, the color becomes locked into the wall, but once the plaster has dried, it no longer absorbs new paint. For this reason, painters spread fresh plaster over only the section of wall they expected to finish in a single day. This practice suggests that a large fresco ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: was usually painted on dry plaster prepared weeks earlier.
choices.B: could be completed by one painter in a single day.
choices.C: was typically painted in sections on different days.
choices.D: used fewer colors than paintings made on wood or canvas.

explanation.why: Painters plastered only as much wall as they could paint in one day, because dry plaster no longer takes paint. A large fresco covers more wall than one day's work, so it must have been built up section by section over many days.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says pigment goes onto fresh, wet plaster; dry plaster no longer absorbs paint.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Each day covered only one section, so a large fresco would take more than one day.
explanation.C: Correct. Since each day's plaster covered only one section, a large work had to be made in many daily sections.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never compares the number of colors in frescoes with other paintings.
